mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% (historical low), or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals weak labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% MoM indicates strong consumer demand, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise above 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals an economic slowdown, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO falls below 100, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% YoY, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0% (annualized), or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion, a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods during early-cycle expansions when UNRATE falls below 4.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.
